elohim.name: Elohim

strongs.gloss: plural of eloah (H433): gods in the ordinary sense; specifically, the supreme God; occasionally applied to magistrates (judges)

elohim.literal: God (a plural form that takes a singular verb when it means the one God)
elohim.short: God, the general Hebrew word for deity
elohim.why: The first name for God in the Bible, and the one in Genesis 1:1. The ending -im is normally a plural, and scholars read it here as a plural of majesty: many in form, one in meaning. The same word is also used in the Hebrew Bible for the gods of other nations.
elohim.use: English Bibles print Elohim as God, so we can count the English word but not the Hebrew one. The English word God also translates the Greek Theos in the New Testament, which is why the Old Testament and New Testament counts are split below.
faq: Is Elohim plural?

Elohim is plural in form (the -im ending), and Strong's lists it as the plural of eloah. When it names the one God it takes a singular verb, which is why scholars call it a plural of majesty. In Genesis 1:1 the verb "created" is singular.
Is Elohim the same as Yahweh?
No. Elohim is a title meaning God. Yahweh (rendered LORD in the KJV) is the personal name God gives in Exodus 3. The two appear together as "LORD God" from Genesis 2:4.

adonai.name: Adonai

strongs.gloss: the Lord (used as a proper name of God only); short definition: Lord, Master

adonai.short: my Lord, a title of respect and rule
adonai.why: Adonai comes from adon (lord, master; Strong's: sovereign, controller, human or divine). The form is a plural of rank with the ending for "my", literally "my lords", and it is used of God alone. Jewish readers say Adonai aloud wherever the written text has the name YHWH, so the word became the spoken stand-in for the name.
adonai.use: English Bibles print Adonai as Lord, in ordinary capitals, and print the name YHWH as LORD in small capitals. The same Lord also translates the Greek Kyrios in the New Testament, so a count of the word Lord cannot isolate Adonai and we leave that count out. The one pattern English text does mark is Adonai followed by YHWH, printed Lord GOD in the KJV and Lord Yahweh in the World English Bible.
faq: What does Adonai mean?
Adonai means "my Lord". It comes from adon (master, lord) with the ending for "my", and Strong's lists it as the Lord, used as a proper name of God only.
Why does the Bible print Lord GOD?

Lord GOD marks the Hebrew words Adonai YHWH together. The KJV prints the first in ordinary capitals and the second in capitals so a reader can tell them apart; GOD stands in for the name instead of repeating LORD.
How do you pronounce Adonai?
Adonai is pronounced ah-doh-NYE, with the stress on the last syllable.

el-shaddai.name: El Shaddai

strongs.gloss: God, god, mighty one
the Almighty (from shadad)

el-shaddai.why: El Shaddai is the name God uses with Abraham in Genesis 17:1 and the name the patriarchs knew him by, according to Exodus 6:3. Strong's gives Shaddai as coming from shadad; where the word comes from is still debated.
el-shaddai.use: Both the KJV and the World English Bible translate El Shaddai as God Almighty, and translate Shaddai on its own as the Almighty, mostly in Job. The KJV also prints Almighty God where the World English Bible has God Almighty, and the New Testament uses the same English for the Greek Pantokrator, so the New Testament counts below are not El Shaddai.
faq: What does El Shaddai mean?
El Shaddai means "God Almighty". El is the Hebrew word for God (Strong's H410, strength or mighty one) and Shaddai is translated the Almighty (H7706).
Where is El Shaddai first used?
God introduces himself as El Shaddai to Abram in Genesis 17:1, when Abram was ninety-nine, the first verse where the World English Bible has God Almighty.

jehovah.name: Jehovah
jehovah.translit: YHWH (yĕhōvâ), written Jehovah in the KJV

strongs.gloss: (the) self-Existent or Eternal; Jehovah, Jewish national name of God

jehovah.short: LORD, the personal name of God
jehovah.why: Jehovah is how the KJV prints the four Hebrew letters YHWH, God's personal name. The form Jehovah is a later blend of those consonants with the vowels of Adonai; most scholars think the original pronunciation was closer to Yahweh. The KJV uses Jehovah only a few times and prints LORD in capitals everywhere else.
jehovah.use: Counting the KJV's capitals gives the closest English count of the name, and the World English Bible, which writes Yahweh each time, gives an independent count. The two translations word the name differently, so each count is shown on its own and not added together.
faq: What does Jehovah mean?
Jehovah is the English form of YHWH, God's personal name. Strong's glosses it as the self-existent or eternal one, which matches God's reply in Exodus 3:14, "I AM WHO I AM".
Is Jehovah the same as Yahweh?
Yes. Both stand for the Hebrew letters YHWH. Yahweh is the reconstructed pronunciation most scholars prefer, and Jehovah is the older English form that the KJV uses.
Why does the KJV say LORD instead of Jehovah?
The KJV follows the Jewish custom of reading Adonai (Lord) aloud in place of the name, and marks the name with LORD in capitals. It prints the name itself only a few times.

yahweh.name: Yahweh

strongs.gloss: (the) self-Existent or Eternal; Jehovah, Jewish national name of God
Jah, the sacred name

yahweh.short: the personal name of God, as the World English Bible writes it
yahweh.why: Yahweh is the modern scholarly way of saying YHWH, the name God gives Moses at the burning bush. The World English Bible uses it every time the Hebrew text has the name, where the KJV prints LORD. It is the same name as Jehovah, which has its own page.
yahweh.use: Because the World English Bible writes the name out, the word Yahweh can be counted directly. The shortened form Yah, found in Hallelujah (praise Yah), is counted separately.
faq: What does Yahweh mean?
Yahweh means "he is" or "the self-existent one". Strong's glosses the name as the self-existent or eternal.
Where does the Bible first say Yahweh?
The first verse where the World English Bible uses Yahweh is Genesis 2:4, in the phrase "Yahweh God".

jehovah-jireh.name: Jehovah Jireh

strongs.gloss: Jehovah will see (to it); Jehovah-Jireh, a symbolical name for Mount Moriah

jehovah-jireh.literal: the LORD will see to it; the LORD will provide
jehovah-jireh.why: Abraham gives this name to the place where God supplied a ram in place of Isaac. Yireh is a form of the verb to see, so the name reads "the LORD will see". Genesis 22:8 explains the sense: "God will provide himself a lamb", where provide is the same verb, to see ahead and supply.
jehovah-jireh.use: The name appears once. The KJV transliterates it as Jehovah-jireh and the World English Bible translates it as Yahweh Will Provide, so the same verse is the only match in each Bible.
faq: What does Jehovah Jireh mean?
Jehovah Jireh means "the LORD will see to it", usually put as "the LORD will provide". Strong's glosses H3070 as Jehovah will see (to it).
Where is Jehovah Jireh in the Bible?
Only in Genesis 22:14, where Abraham names the mountain after God provided a ram in place of his son Isaac.

jehovah-rapha.name: Jehovah Rapha

strongs.gloss: (the) self-Existent or Eternal; Jehovah, Jewish national name of God
(properly) to mend (by stitching), i.e. (figuratively) to cure; to heal, restore

jehovah-rapha.why: Jehovah Rapha is not a name printed anywhere in the text. It is drawn from Exodus 15:26, where God says "I am the LORD that healeth thee", in Hebrew YHWH rophe'ka, using the participle of rapha, to heal. Bible teachers began calling it a name of God because of that verse, and it is now a common worship phrase.
jehovah-rapha.use: We searched both Bibles for the name written out and it never appears: the count is zero in each. What the text does contain is the sentence in Exodus 15:26, which is why this page counts that wording instead.
faq: What does Jehovah Rapha mean?
Jehovah Rapha means "the LORD who heals". Rapha (Strong's H7495) means to mend or heal, and the phrase comes from God's words to Israel in Exodus 15:26.
Is Jehovah Rapha a name in the Bible?
Not as a printed name. The phrase is built from Exodus 15:26, "I am the LORD that healeth thee"; neither the KJV nor the World English Bible prints Jehovah-rapha.

strongs.gloss: Jehovah (is) my banner; Jehovah-Nissi, a symbolical name of an altar

jehovah-nissi.why: Moses names an altar Jehovah-nissi after Israel beats Amalek at Rephidim. Nes, the word behind nissi, is a banner or standard raised on a pole as a rallying point, so the name says that God is the banner Israel gathers under. The World English Bible puts it as "Yahweh our Banner".
jehovah-nissi.use: The name occurs once in each Bible, in the same verse. Where the KJV leaves the Hebrew in transliteration, the World English Bible translates it.
faq: What does Jehovah Nissi mean?
Jehovah Nissi means "the LORD is my banner". Strong's glosses H3071 as Jehovah (is) my banner.
Where is Jehovah Nissi in the Bible?
Only in Exodus 17:15, where Moses builds an altar and gives it this name after the battle with Amalek.

jehovah-shalom.name: Jehovah Shalom

strongs.gloss: Jehovah (is) peace; Jehovah-Shalom, a symbolical name of an altar
peace, completeness, welfare, well-being, safety, prosperity

jehovah-shalom.why: Gideon builds an altar at Ophrah and names it Jehovah-shalom after the angel of the LORD tells him he will not die. Shalom means more than the absence of war: Strong's lists completeness, welfare, safety and prosperity as well as peace.
jehovah-shalom.use: The name occurs once. The KJV transliterates it and the World English Bible translates it, "Yahweh is Peace", both in Judges 6:24.
faq: What does Jehovah Shalom mean?
Jehovah Shalom means "the LORD is peace". Shalom (Strong's H7965) covers wholeness and welfare as well as peace.
Where is Jehovah Shalom in the Bible?
Judges 6:24 is the only verse. Gideon names his altar after hearing "Peace be unto thee; fear not" in the verse before.

strongs.gloss: Jehovah (is) thither; Jehovah-Shammah, a symbolic title of Jerusalem

jehovah-shammah.why: Jehovah Shammah is the name Ezekiel gives to the restored city in the last verse of his book. Shammah is the Hebrew for "there", so the name answers the vision that began with God's glory leaving the temple: the city's name is that he is back.
jehovah-shammah.use: The Hebrew name is not transliterated in either Bible. Both translate it as a sentence, so this page counts that sentence.
faq: What does Jehovah Shammah mean?
Jehovah Shammah means "the LORD is there". Strong's glosses H3074 as Jehovah (is) thither, and the verse renders it "The LORD is there".
Where is Jehovah Shammah in the Bible?
Ezekiel 48:35, the closing verse of the book, gives it as the name of the city.

jehovah-sabaoth.name: Jehovah Sabaoth

strongs.gloss: (the) self-Existent or Eternal; Jehovah, Jewish national name of God
a mass of persons, especially regularly organized for war (an army); hosts

jehovah-sabaoth.why: The LORD of hosts is the name of God as commander of armies, human and heavenly. It first appears in 1 Samuel 1:3 and is common in the prophets. Sabaoth is the Hebrew word for hosts written in Greek letters: Paul quotes Isaiah with it in Romans 9:29, and James uses it in James 5:4.
jehovah-sabaoth.use: The KJV prints LORD of hosts, and the World English Bible prints Yahweh of Armies. Both are counted, and the different totals show how each translation words the same Hebrew phrase.
faq: What does Jehovah Sabaoth mean?
Jehovah Sabaoth means "the LORD of hosts", or "of armies". Tsaba (Strong's H6635) is an army or host, organized especially for war.
Where is Jehovah Sabaoth first used?
In 1 Samuel 1:3, where Elkanah goes up to worship "the LORD of hosts" at Shiloh.

el-elyon.name: El Elyon

strongs.gloss: God, god, mighty one
an elevation, i.e. (adj.) lofty; as title, the Supreme; most high

el-elyon.why: El Elyon is the title Melchizedek, king of Salem, carries as priest in Genesis 14. Abram uses it in the same chapter to swear to the king of Sodom, where he adds the LORD, tying the Most High God to Yahweh. Elyon comes from a word for high, so the title means God above all.
el-elyon.use: The KJV prints most high God, the World English Bible prints God Most High, and both are counted. The English phrase also covers the Aramaic of Daniel and the Greek of Mark and Acts, so the Old Testament and New Testament counts are split.
faq: What does El Elyon mean?
El Elyon means "God Most High". Elyon (Strong's H5945) comes from a word for elevation or height and is used as a name for the Supreme God.
Who first called God El Elyon?
Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest, in Genesis 14:18-20, when he blessed Abram.

el-roi.name: El Roi

strongs.gloss: God, god, mighty one
seeing, vision, sight

el-roi.literal: the God who sees me (God of seeing)
el-roi.why: Hagar, running from Sarai into the wilderness, hears from the angel of the LORD and names him the God who sees her. The Hebrew roi is seeing, so the name means God of seeing, and the well is called Beer-lahai-roi in the next verse.
el-roi.use: The Hebrew name is not transliterated in the KJV or the World English Bible; both translate Hagar's words in Genesis 16:13. The well named for it is counted separately.
faq: What does El Roi mean?
El Roi means "the God who sees me". Roi (Strong's H7210) is seeing or a sight, so the name reads God of seeing.
Who named God El Roi?
Hagar, in Genesis 16:13, after the angel of the LORD found her by a spring in the wilderness.

el-olam.name: El Olam

strongs.gloss: God, god, mighty one
properly, concealed, i.e. the vanishing point; time out of mind, i.e. (practically) eternity

el-olam.why: Abraham calls on El Olam at Beersheba in Genesis 21:33 after making peace with Abimelech. Olam is a word for time out of mind, stretching to the farthest past or future, so the name says that God is not bounded by time. Isaiah 40:28 repeats the thought: "the everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth".
el-olam.use: English text can only follow the translation: the KJV prints everlasting God and eternal God, and the World English Bible uses the same two, so both phrases are counted. Romans 16:26 has the same English for the Greek, so the Old Testament split matters.
faq: What does El Olam mean?
El Olam means "the everlasting God" or "the eternal God". Olam (Strong's H5769) is time out of mind, eternity.
Where is El Olam in the Bible?
Genesis 21:33 is the verse: Abraham plants a tree at Beersheba and calls on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God.
